newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Charter freighters needed for some cargo routes.
newsitem.headline: Charter freighters needed for some cargo routes.

text.p: Charter freighter aircraft will come into their own to provide capacity on some cargo routes, because passenger traffic is increasingly influenced by tourism and leisure demands, Emirates senior general manager cargo, Ram C.Menen said on Tuesday.
"Freighters will come into their own. They'll plough the commerce and trade routes, further triggering global commercial activity," he told the Asian Air cargo summit.
Investment by airlines in this area is likely to trigger further changes in the world distribution process, leading to almost a revolution in trade patterns and the global market, Menen added.
Dense commercial routes and seasonal traffic flows require more lift capability than that offered by scheduled carriers, thus providing a role for charter freighters.
Additionally, those "routes which cannot be served by widebodied aircraft cannot be left out of expanding world trade," and charter is the answer to their needs, he added.

Industry forecasts for world cargo growth suggest that certain cargo routes will be candidates for such charter traffic and these include, "the CIS/Africa, intra-Far East trade and Europe-South America," he said.

Menen also said that while cargo yields are expected to continue to decline at around one percent a year, "the positive side of the decline in yields is that lower valued goods tend to take to the air as it becomes more affordable."

Once this shift happens, "there is a growth in volumes... and these are expected to replace unit profitability. Contract traffic has become the order of the day" providing adequate business for shipper,forwarder and the airlines. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
